<p class="hero-statement">Institutions, power, and the <em>long reach of history.</em></p>

::: {.hairline-section .about-intro}
<div class="section-index">01 <span>/</span> ABOUT</div>

::: {.about-grid}
::: {.about-heading}
## Politics is shaped by institutions—and by the histories behind them. {.display-heading}
:::

::: {.about-body}
My research examines the development of state institutions, their relationships with local actors, and the long-term consequences of political conflict. I am especially interested in why states respond differently to local demands and how earlier forms of political incorporation continue to matter.

My empirical approach combines historical data collection with quantitative methods, including natural experiments, panel data, Bayesian statistics, and language models.

[More about my work <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span>](research.html){.text-link}
:::
:::
:::

### Exams, Elites, and the Local State {.paper-title}

*Bureaucratic Incorporation and Territorial Governance in Joseon Korea*

Examines how local access to the central bureaucracy relates to the territorial distribution of state relief in premodern Korea.

### A Funeral Without End {.paper-title}

*The Political Legacy of the May 18 Democratization Movement in South Korea*

Investigates the long-run electoral consequences of state violence and democratization in South Korea.
:::
<div class="paper-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↗</div>

*Transfer Learning for Political Text Classification*

Studies how political text classification tools transfer across languages and political contexts, including Korean-language adaptation.
